title: Check if a string is substring of another - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given two strings txt and pat, return the 0-based index of the first occurrence of the substring pat in txt. If pat is not found, return -1.

Examples: 

Input: txt = "GeeksForGeeks", pat = "Fr"
Output: -1
Explanation: "Fr" is not present in the string "GeeksForGeeks" as substring.

Input: txt = "GeeksForGeeks", pat = "For"
Output: 5
Explanation: "For" is present as substring in "GeeksForGeeks" from index 5 (0 based indexing).

Input: txt = "GeeksForGeeks", pat = "gr"
Output: -1
Explanation: "gr" is not present in the string "GeeksForGeeks" as substring.

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • Nested loops - O(n * m) Time and O(1) Space
  • Pattern Searching Algorithms - O(n + m) Time
  • In-built library functions

Nested loops - O(n * m) Time and O(1) Space

The basic idea is to traverse the string txt and check whether pat matches starting from each index. For every index, use a nested loop to compare the characters of pat with the corresponding characters of txt.

  • If all characters of pat match, return the starting index.
  • If a mismatch occurs, move to the next index of txt.
  • Return -1 if pat is not found in txt.
C++ 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

// Function to find if pat is a substring of txt
int firstOccurence(string &txt, string &pat)
{
    int n = txt.length();
    int m = pat.length();

    // Iterate through txt
    for (int i = 0; i <= n - m; i++)
    {

        // Check for substring match
        int j;
        for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
        {

            // Mismatch found
            if (txt[i + j] != pat[j])
            {
                break;
            }
        }

        // If we completed the inner loop, we found a match
        if (j == m)
        {

            // Return starting index
            return i;
        }
    }

    // No match found
    return -1;
}

int main()
{
    string txt = "GeeksForGeeks";
    string pat = "For";

    cout << firstOccurence(txt, pat);

    return 0;
}

def firstOccurence(txt, pat):
    n = len(txt)
    m = len(pat)

    # Iterate through txt
    for i in range(n - m + 1):

        # Check for substring match
        j = 0
        while j < m and txt[i + j] == pat[j]:
            j += 1
        
        # If we completed the inner loop, we found a match
        if j == m:
            return i

    # No match found
    return -1

Pattern Searching Algorithms - O(n + m) Time

There are several pattern searching algorithms, such as:

  • KMP Algorithm,
  • Rabin-Karp Algorithm,
  • Aho-Corasick Algorithm,

Please refer to Introduction to Pattern Searching to learn more about them.

In-built library functions

This approach uses a built-in function to find the first occurrence of pat in txt.

Most programming languages provide built-in functions to find the first occurrence of a substring. The commonly used functions are:

  • C: strstr()
  • C++: string::find()
  • Java: String.indexOf()
  • Python: str.find()
  • C#: String.IndexOf()
  • JavaScript: String.indexOf()
C++ 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int firstOccurence(string &txt, string &pat)
{
    // Find the first occurrence of pat in txt.
    size_t idx = txt.find(pat);

    // Return the index if pat is found, otherwise return -1.
    if (idx != string::npos)
        return idx;

    return -1;
}

int main()
{
    string txt = "GeeksForGeeks";
    string pat = "For";

    cout << firstOccurence(txt, pat);

    return 0;
}
C 
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int firstOccurence(char *txt, char *pat)
{
    // Find the first occurrence of pat in txt.
    char *idx = strstr(txt, pat);

    // Return the index if pat is found, otherwise return -1.
    if (idx != NULL)
        return (int)(idx - txt);

    return -1;
}

int main()
{
    char txt[] = "GeeksForGeeks";
    char pat[] = "For";

    printf("%d", firstOccurence(txt, pat));

    return 0;
}
